question: What is the medical name for normal earwax?
explanation: Cerumen is just the fancy medical word for the natural wax our ears make to keep things clean and protected. You've got this!

question: Why would a nurse need to flush or irrigate a patient's ear?

options.A: To drain excessive fluid from the middle ear cavity
options.B: To remove stuck earwax or small foreign objects
options.C: To repair a torn eardrum using pressurized water
options.D: To treat an active bacterial infection deep in the inner ear

explanation: Ear irrigation is a safe way to wash out stubborn wax buildup or little things that got stuck in the outer ear. Great clinical thinking!

question: When should you NEVER perform an ear irrigation?

options.B: Mild itching in the outer ear
options.C: A history of mild seasonal allergies

explanation: Never put fluid into an ear with a hole in the eardrum! It can push water and infection straight into the middle ear. Safety first!

question: A patient comes in with a small plastic bead stuck in their ear, but no pain. What is your very first step?

options.A: Immediately begin high-pressure irrigation to wash out the bead
options.B: Send the patient home without an examination
options.C: Instill cold water to freeze the plastic bead so it shrinks
options.D: Check the ear with an otoscope to look at the eardrum first

explanation: Always take a peek with your otoscope first! You need to make sure the eardrum is safe and intact before you introduce any water.

question: How warm should the water be when you prepare it for ear irrigation?
explanation: Using lukewarm water matches body temperature. It keeps the patient comfortable and prevents terrible dizziness!

question: What happens if you accidentally use cold water to flush a patient's ear?

options.A: The earwax will instantly dissolve into liquid
options.B: The eardrum will automatically seal itself tighter
options.C: The patient may feel very dizzy and start vomiting
options.D: The water flow will stop completely

explanation: Cold water messes with the balance organs in the inner ear, triggering heavy dizziness and nausea (vertigo). Keep it warm!

question: How do you correctly straighten an adult's ear canal before flushing it?

options.A: Push the tragus inward over the opening
options.B: Tilt the head sharply toward the chest
options.D: Pull the outer ear (pinna) upward and backward

explanation: For adults, pulling the pinna up and back straightens out the curvy ear canal so your water stream can reach the blockage easily.

question: Where should you aim the stream of water inside the ear canal?

options.A: Straight down the bottom floor of the canal
options.B: Directly at the center of the eardrum
options.C: Against the center of the wax plug only
options.D: Against the top or back wall of the canal

explanation: Aiming along the canal wall lets the water slip behind the wax and push it out gently, without blasting the delicate eardrum.

question: What is your immediate action if the patient feels sharp pain while you are flushing their ear?

options.A: Push the syringe faster to clear the blockage
options.B: Lower the temperature of the water
options.C: Stop the irrigation procedure right away
options.D: Ask the patient to lie flat on the bed

explanation: Pain is a warning sign of injury! Stop immediately to protect your patient from further harm. You're doing great learning this.

question: What damage can happen if you push water into the ear canal with too much force?

options.A: Permanent loss of the sense of taste
options.C: Complete closure of the outer jaw bone
options.D: Instant growth of new ear cartilage

explanation: Too much pressure in a tight space can rupture the thin eardrum. Always use gentle, controlled pressure!

question: Which of these details is NOT needed in your nursing notes after an ear irrigation?

options.A: How the ear canal looked afterward
options.B: The amount and temperature of the fluid used
options.C: The brand name of the plastic syringe used
options.D: How well the patient tolerated the procedure

explanation: You need to document clinical facts like fluid amounts and patient reactions, but nobody needs to know the syringe brand name!

question: Why do nurses check the ear canal with an otoscope after finishing an irrigation?

options.A: To check if the patient's hearing loss is permanent
options.B: To measure the exact length of the ear canal
options.C: To pump remaining air out of the middle ear space
options.D: To make sure the wax or object is actually gone

explanation: An otoscope check lets you double-check your work and confirm the ear canal is clean and the eardrum looks safe. Perfect finish!
